exclusion_detail: Lead disulfide-BPI (6) is made from compound 4, whose synthesis is 'carried out according to the previously described procedure [ref 20]' with no procedure here; 4 itself descends from bacteriopurpurin 1, obtained by allomerisation of bacteriochlorophyll-a produced by Rhodobacter capsulatus (a biological source, not a purchased material). Only the cysteamine/EEDQ coupling and air oxidation of 4 are described.

lead.label: 6 (disulfide-BPI)
lead.why: Abstract: the dipropoxy-BPI was 'readily oxidized in oxygen atmosphere yielding the corresponding disulfide analogue (disulfide-BPI)'; it is the compound used for CC50, singlet oxygen and in vivo PDT studies.

notes: Macrocyclic tetrapyrrole derived from a natural bacteriochlorophyll source.
